Realised mean and variance of a zero-truncated count distribution

Source: R/counts.R
uptake_moments.Rd

LAMBDA_OOCYSTS / LAMBDA_SPOROZOITES are pre-truncation rates, so they are not the mean count you would read off a paper: conditioning away the zeros pulls the realised mean up. This returns what the model actually produces for a given lambda (and dispersion k), so you can check a parameter choice against a reported figure.

Usage

uptake_moments(lambda, k = 0)

Arguments

lambda

pre-truncation mean (> 0).

k

dispersion; 0 (default) = Poisson, > 0 = negative binomial.

Value

named numeric of mean and var (the realised, zero-truncated values).

Details

With base mean \(\lambda\), dispersion \(k\) and zero-probability \(p_0\), the truncated moments are \(E[X] = \lambda/(1-p_0)\) and \(Var[X] = E[X^2]/(1-p_0) - E[X]^2\). k <= 0 is Poisson (\(p_0 = e^{-\lambda}\)); k > 0 is negative binomial with \(Var = \lambda + \lambda^2/k\) and \(p_0 = (k/(k+\lambda))^k\).

See also

uptake_calibrate() for the inverse (target moments -> lambda, k).

Examples

uptake_moments(2)          # Poisson lambda = 2 -> realised mean ~2.31
#>     mean      var 
#> 2.313035 1.588974 
uptake_moments(2, k = 1)   # negative binomial, same lambda -> realised mean ~3.0, more spread
#> mean  var 
#>    3    6
